data.name: The Quarantined Archive
data.description: A chart marks a chamber missing from every ship plan. Someone aboard the Ghost Ship once tried to quarantine what the Core was getting wrong, and filed it behind three seals. A wrong answer at any seal trips the alarm: you fight the archive's guard, then continue. Answer all three cleanly for the better haul.
data.successDescription: The archive's last seal is broken and its records are yours.

objectives.description: The upward seal channels hold the ship aloft. A thinner line runs against their flow, carrying fragments of handwriting and fractured memories toward a sealed section inside the hull. Someone once tried to isolate a failure from the main network.

nextObjectiveId.text: Follow the breach into the hull

objectives.description: Below the waterline the hull is rebuilding itself from timber and cable that do not belong together. Something large is being rebuilt with them, and it is not finished.

nextObjectiveId.text: Face what the hull is building

objectives.description: The Core Horror pulls itself out of the frame.
objectives.failDescription: You are driven back. Catch your breath and try again.
objectives.drawDescription: Neither side gives way. Try again.

objectives.description: You were beaten back. The fight waits for you.
With the Core Horror defeated, the surrounding frame begins sketching its ruined body again. Beneath the ladder, a severed impression conduit pulses toward a sealed maintenance chamber.

Rows of framed seal patterns stand without occupants. Each carries a human impression, not a living body: a remembered greeting, the shape of a hand reaching for warm tea, a command repeated until its meaning has faded. A small maintenance plate is locked behind the frames.
You choose: Force the Captain's command seal. The seal flares red and the archive's alarm begins to toll.
You choose: Override the lift lattice. The seal flares red and the archive's alarm begins to toll.

First seal. Three seal paths remain on the plate. One rises to the lift network, one bears the Captain's command mark, and a third turns back beneath the inactive frames. Beside the return path someone scratched: 'What command cannot repair must first be quarantined.'

nextObjectiveId.text: Trace the return seal beneath the frames

objectives.description: You were beaten back. The fight waits for you.
The last seal opens a narrow chamber not marked on any ship plan. Command records and damaged crew impressions were moved here and filed as containment faults. Their custodian has not yet appeared.
The alarm dies as you cross into the archive, too late to matter. Command records and damaged crew impressions were filed here as containment faults. Their custodian already knows you are coming.

The reports span decades. Each warns that reconstructed patterns are deteriorating while preservation remains mandatory. The same seal-engineer's signature appears on every revision, although no living engineer could have filed them all. The final correction is stamped 'Access refused by command priority.'

A senior shinobi engineer gathers from the engraved lines, his form steadier than the damaged crew below. 'I sealed the worst of it away,' the Sealwright says. 'Command would not permit me to stop the work. It will not permit you to take these records.' He raises a sealing stance.
The Sealwright is waiting, already in his sealing stance. 'You came through my alarms,' he says. 'Then you know what this place is for.'
Break the Sealwright's containment defense.

The archive is yours, though the alarms cost you. You leave with what the custodian could not keep.

data.name: The Captain's Watch
data.description: The Captain's impression still keeps the night watch, and he never refuses a challenger. But the Oathkeeper sets terms: before each fight you may accept a handicap. Every term you take and survive raises the haul. A lost fight is retried with the same terms.
data.successDescription: You kept the Captain's watch and claimed its stores.

objectives.description: The chart's route ends at a cove where the Ghost Ship's boat is drawn up on the sand, waiting. The Oathkeeper stands beside it. 'The Captain keeps the night watch,' he says. 'He will meet you. I set the terms.'
In the chart room the Wayfinder looks up from decades of corrections. The Oathkeeper speaks from the doorway: 'Fight him without your foreign seal-work, and the Captain will hear of it.'
You refuse the term. The Wayfinder redraws the room around you.
Your seal-work goes quiet. The Wayfinder waits.
The Wayfinder redraws the room around you.
